title: Mixed-sequence tail latency regression — 2025-09-18 sync
content:
Summary:
- Quick sync to hand off the mixed-sequence tail latency regression investigation (p99 spikes under mixed short/long sequence traffic).
- Short version: after the routing heuristic change last week that prefers model-variant-B for sequences >512 tokens, we see reproducible p99 spikes (~1.6s) under a 90% short / 10% long mixed workload. Baseline (all-short) p99 ~480ms; mixed-run p99 ~1.6s.

Attendees:
- Aisha Patel (owner)
- Marco Li (bench infra)
- Sofia Nguyen (runtime kernels)
- Ethan Brooks (SRE)
- Priya Raman (product / rollouts)

Context / why this matters:
- The regression affects Dedicated customers with mixed traffic patterns; it appears intermittently in Hosted too. It increases observed tail latency and causes transient error rates for time-sensitive routes. We need action before next week’s canary expansion.

Observed signals (aggregate from 3 runs, 09/18):
- Workload: mix 90/10 short:long (short=64 tokens, long=1024 tokens), target QPS=200, duration=20m.
- Baseline (no routing change) run: p50=85ms, p95=290ms, p99=480ms, throughput=195 qps, GPU util=72%
- Mixed run (routing heuristic enabled): p50=90ms, p95=320ms, p99=1600ms, throughput=188 qps, GPU util=58% (drops observed during spikes)
- Trace samples show long queuing on the inference worker (agent-side) prior to kernel execution, plus intermittent KV-cache miss storms for long sequences when they arrive after bursts of short seqs.
- Agent logs: spikes in "inflight-batches" and increased serialization_time on RPC layer.
- Representative trace: https://console.redwood.ai/trace/trace-2025-09-18-7b3f (span waterfall shows 1.1s queue + 0.4s kernel exec)

Repro steps (how we ran the bench):
1) Checkout bench harness: git checkout refs/pull/bench/2025-09-mix-test
2) Command used: ./bench --qps 200 --duration 20m --mix "short:90,64;long:10,1024" --model blue-1b-variantA --route-policy heuristic-v2
3) Captured runtime metrics via /metrics endpoint and traces via distributed tracer.
4) Repeated 3 times across two racks (eu-west-2a, eu-west-2b).

Hypotheses discussed:
- H1: KV-cache thrash — long sequences bypass/evict prefix caches causing subsequent short requests to miss and rebuild KVs (costly for mixed workload). Evidence: cache-miss spikes correlate with queue growth.
- H2: Batching heterogeneity overhead — mixing long and short in the same batch forces padding/extra kernel paths, increasing per-token overhead for some batches. Evidence: kernel selector logs show fallback to generic kernel when mixed sizes present.
- H3: RPC serialization stalls — current agent serializes some batch prep steps on a single goroutine; a long request holding the prep lock delays subsequent batched requests. Evidence: "serialization_time" metric spikes.
- H4: Model-variant switch mismatch — routing to variant-B triggers a different kernel path with slower init for first long sequence after a short-burst, causing warmup stalls. Evidence: variant-B warmup traces shorter but present.

Notes from profiling (Sofia):
- Kernel logs show increased calls to generic_attention path when sequences >512 are present in the same batch as short sequences. That path has higher overhead; we should quantify cost of separating batches by sequence length.
- Captured small flamegraphs: CPU on agent increases ~30% during spike windows.

Experiment matrix proposed (agreed):
- E1: Isolate batching: run bench with "per-seq-length batching" flag enabled (group by length before batching). Expectation: reduces p99 if batching heterogeneity is root cause. Owner: Marco.
- E2: KV-cache stress: synthetic test that issues long seqs at low qps while short seqs flood to observe eviction patterns. Capture KV metrics (hit/miss, eviction). Owner: Aisha.
- E3: Agent concurrency tweak: increase worker-pool size and remove single serialization point in prep. Quick experiment to see if serialization_time drop reduces queueing. Owner: Ethan.
- E4: Rollback routing policy in canary to previous heuristic (v1) for one customer slice while we test. Owner: Priya.

Immediate action items (owners & ETA):
- Marco: run E1 across two racks, collect histograms and kernel-selector logs; due 2025-09-19 EOD.
- Aisha: run E2 with KV instrumentation (enable kv.debug=true), capture eviction traces and produce CSV of hit/miss per minute; due 2025-09-19 noon.
- Sofia: add lightweight metric export for kernel-path counts (generic_attention vs optimized_one) in nightly canary; due 2025-09-20.
- Ethan: prototype agent prep concurrency fix (PR draft) to remove lock hotspot; aim for bench-enabled PR by 2025-09-22.
- Priya: schedule canary rollback for affected customer slice (config rollback) if we see more than one recurrence in next 48h; coordinate with SRE.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How much of the p99 is kernel exec vs queueing? (we have traces showing ~1.1s queue + 0.4s exec but need more samples).
- Does moving to per-seq-length batching materially increase overall cost (smaller batches for long sequences)? need cost estimate.
- Is there a simple routing policy (e.g., route all long sequences to variant-B but use a separate dedicated queue or worker pool) that provides isolation without major infra changes?

Quick debugging artifacts (snippets):
- Example agent log around t=12:14:22:
  [12:14:22.433] inflight-batches=34 queue_size=128 serialization_time_ms=312 kernel_path=generic_attention
  [12:14:22.837] trace_id=7b3f span=prep serialize_wait=310ms exec=398ms

- Benchmark command (for reproduction):
  ./bench --qps 200 --duration 20m --mix "short:90,64;long:10,1024" --model blue-1b --route-policy heuristic-v2 --collect-traces

Notes to self (Aisha):
- when running E2, capture both agent-level and serving-node KV metrics; correlate by minute.
- add a quick script to compute "mixed-batch fraction" (how many batches contain both short and long).

Decision criteria (for rollback / mitigation):
- If p99 > 1s for 2 of 3 runs at QPS >= 150 on prod-like infra, trigger immediate rollback for canary.
- If E1 reduces p99 by >40% without >10% throughput loss, prefer batching isolation approach.

Slack threads / references:
- Slack: #serving-runtime "mixed-seq-p99" (links: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C02ABC1234/p1695030000000)
- PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/789
- Jira: INF-3421 (mixed-sequence p99 regression)

Next sync:
- Quick standup tomorrow 09/19 10:00 UTC to review E1/E2 preliminary results.

Bottom line: the regression is reproducible and seems tied to batching + routing interactions; short-term mitigations (per-length batching, small agent concurrency fixes, or temporary routing rollback) are all viable. We need bench data to pick the least-cost, low-risk path.

---
Keywords for search: mixed sequence, batching heterogeneity, kv-cache thrash, agent serialization, p99 surge, routing heuristic, variant-B, per-length batching
